source_excerpts.text:
I have not constructed the full processor in your question. I also have not proved an obstruction to that model. The unresolved step is passive retention from the output of a physically noisy writer—and recovery of that same retention guarantee after a native gate. The thermal-encoding memory theorem does not supply this step.

I did obtain a constructive classical thermal-syndrome sampler, an exact reference-safe reduction of HOLD errors to a syndrome process, and a local-noise bound derived from the actual Davies dissipator during active controls. I also constructed exact counterexamples to two tempting ways of completing the missing retention proof. These are substantive results, but they do not establish the requested processor threshold.

The complete derivations, conditions, finite certificates and inherited access notes are saved here:


- 3D_THERMAL_PROCESSOR_RETURN.txt <https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_dbc1b41cd8e481919d27ef9337c0cec7&account_id=personal>
- P3_3D_THERMAL_PROCESSOR_20261108.zip <https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_f3a6676622a481918b0a4201010f3b98&account_id=personal>


1. What the construction currently establishes

I used the proved three-dimensional code family, retaining its thermal logical encoding and its actual embedding construction. I did not substitute the simpler explicit embedding whose lifetime is left unproved. The source’s noisy-initialization and non-Clifford-processing gaps remain material. arxiv.org+1 <https://arxiv.org/html/2605.10943v1?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

The status of the operational components is:





Component | Result established here | Remaining physical requirement | 
Thermal syndrome acquisition | A bounded-execution classical sampler with polynomial work at an explicitly chosen temperature | Physical preparation still suffers release faults | 
HOLD channel | An exact diamond-error reduction valid for arbitrary references and syndrome–logical correlations | A long-time bound for the syndrome law actually released by WRITE/GATE | 
Bath during active controls | A local-norm fault bound derived from the unchanged Davies generator | A complete native fault-tolerance argument using that bound | 
Native recovery and gates | Exact recovery-teleportation channel identities with clean encoded resources | Noisy resource preparation, terminal faults and return to a retainable state class |
